summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her 15th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well with only mild nausea, managed with anti-emetics. Methotrexate cleared appropriately with no renal or hepatic toxicity. An MRI showed stable lymphoma without new lesions. Her dyspnea was attributed to acute bronchitis, and she improved with a new albuterol-ipratropium inhaler. Aspirin was held during admission to enhance methotrexate excretion and was restarted at discharge. She remained stable emotionally, denying depression or suicidal ideation, and was discharged home in good condition with follow-up instructions.
problems: Other malignant lymphomas, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
